stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: In much of the Corn Belt, fields sit bare between the autumn harvest and spring planting, exposed to wind and heavy rain. Agronomists have found that sowing cereal rye in those fields after harvest changes this. The rye's dense roots bind soil particles together, and its leaves shield the ground from the direct impact of raindrops. ______, fields planted with rye over the winter lose far less topsoil to spring runoff than fields left bare.
explanation: The sentence before the blank explains how rye protects soil: roots bind it and leaves shield it. The sentence after gives the result, which is less topsoil lost. A mechanism followed by its outcome is cause and effect, so "Consequently" is the right choice.

A.why: You chose a contrast word, but the reduced soil loss follows directly from the protection the rye gives. Nothing is being contradicted.

C.why: "Similarly" introduces a second, parallel case. The final sentence isn't a parallel case. It's the result of the mechanism described just before it.

D.why: You read the final sentence as an instance of roots binding soil. It is the effect of that process, not one sample drawn from a larger group.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Biologists reintroduced sea otters to a stretch of rocky coastline expecting the colony to grow steadily for a decade. Instead, its numbers stalled after three years. After two further years of monitoring, the team concluded that one factor above all others was limiting the colony's growth. ______, the shallow kelp beds along that coast supported too few sea urchins, the otters' main prey, to feed more than a few dozen adults.
explanation: The sentence before the blank says that one factor was limiting growth but doesn't name it. The sentence after names that same single factor more precisely. That's specification, not an example, so "Specifically" fits.

A.why: "For example" introduces one case out of several. The passage says there was one factor above all others, so the final sentence names that whole factor. It isn't a sample from a group.

B.why: You chose a contrast word, but the shortage of urchins doesn't push against the team's conclusion. It is that conclusion.

D.why: You reversed the direction of cause. The urchin shortage is what limited the colony. It isn't a result of the team reaching its conclusion.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Health officials in a mid-sized city tested a simple program: parents received automated text messages a week before each of their child's scheduled vaccinations. Over two years, the share of children who completed their vaccinations on time rose by 12 percentage points compared with neighborhoods that received no messages. ______, the program cost the city less than one dollar per family per year, far less than the home-visit programs it had used before.
explanation: The first finding is that the program worked. The second is that it was cheap. Both count in the program's favor, so the second adds to the first. Try it out loud: "it worked, and also it was cheap." That's addition, so "Moreover" is correct.

A.why: A low cost may sound surprising, but it doesn't contradict the program's success. It adds another point in its favor. "However" needs a real reversal.

B.why: Higher vaccination rates didn't cause the low cost. The two facts sit side by side. One doesn't produce the other.

D.why: The cost figure is not an instance of the rise in on-time vaccinations. It's a separate point about the program.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: The Mercator projection, first published in 1569, distorts area badly toward the poles. On a Mercator world map, Greenland looks roughly as large as Africa, even though Africa is about fourteen times bigger. ______, the projection is still standard on nautical charts, because any course that keeps a constant compass bearing appears on it as a straight line, which lets a navigator plot a route with nothing more than a ruler.
explanation: The sentence before the blank gives a serious flaw in the projection. The sentence after says the projection is still widely used anyway. Continued use despite a flaw is the opposite direction, so "Nevertheless" is correct.

A.why: "Thus" would mean the distortion caused the projection's popularity. The passage credits its straight compass lines, not its distortion.

B.why: "Similarly" signals another point in the same direction. The final sentence cuts against the criticism instead of continuing it.

C.why: "Specifically" would restate the distortion more precisely. The final sentence moves to a different point, the projection's value for navigation.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Transcribing a field recording of a traditional singer is painstaking work. The transcriber begins by playing each phrase at half speed, listening for the grace notes and slides that pass too quickly to catch at full tempo. ______, the transcriber writes the phrase in standard notation, adding small symbols above the staff to mark each ornament heard during the slowed playback.
explanation: The passage describes a process in order. The transcriber first listens at half speed and then writes down what they heard. The second sentence simply continues the sequence, so the plain sequence word "Next" is correct. A blank doesn't always need a forceful transition.

A.why: "Instead" means the transcriber replaces slowed listening with notation. The final sentence says the notation records what was "heard during the slowed playback," so both steps happen.

C.why: You chose an opposite-direction word, but writing the notation doesn't oppose the listening. It's the step that comes after it.

D.why: Writing the notation is not an example of listening at half speed. It's the following step in the process.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: A woodcut prints from the raised surface of a carved block. The printmaker rolls ink across the block, and only the uncut wood touches the paper. Every area the artist carves away stays white. ______, an artist who wants a single thin black line cannot simply draw it into the wood but must cut away material on both sides of it, leaving the line standing as a narrow ridge.
explanation: The sentences before the blank set out the rule: only raised wood prints, and carved areas stay white. The final sentence gives what follows from that rule for drawing a black line. A principle followed by its consequence is cause and effect, so "Thus" is correct.

B.why: "Instead" signals a replacement for what came before. Cutting away wood on both sides doesn't replace the principle. It follows from it.

C.why: "Likewise" introduces a parallel case. The thin line isn't a separate, similar situation. It's a result of the rule just described.

D.why: "Admittedly" concedes a point before a reversal, and no reversal follows. The final sentence applies the principle. It doesn't grant a point against it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Saturn's bright rings are famous, but they are not unique. Each of the solar system's four giant planets has a ring system, though most are far fainter than Saturn's. ______, the rings of Uranus are made of material darker than charcoal and went undetected until 1977, when astronomers saw a distant star flicker several times as the planet's rings passed in front of it.
explanation: The sentence before the blank makes a claim about a group: four giant planets, most with faint rings. The sentence after picks out one member of that group, Uranus, to illustrate the claim. One case drawn from several is an example, so "For example" is correct.

A.why: "Specifically" would restate the whole claim more precisely. Uranus is only one of the four giant planets, so the final sentence gives a sample from the group, not a sharper version of the claim.

B.why: You chose a contrast word, but Uranus's dark, hard-to-see rings support the point that most ring systems are faint. They don't contradict it.

D.why: "Similarly" would introduce a new case that parallels the one before. Uranus is not a parallel to the general claim. It's an instance of it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Nutrition researchers tracking the diets of 1,200 schoolchildren wanted to know which foods supplied most of the children's iron. The answer surprised some of them. ______, fortified breakfast cereals are often high in added sugar, and several popular brands exceed recommended limits in a single bowl. But for the children in this study, those cereals provided more iron than any other food, including red meat and leafy greens.
explanation: The sentence after the blank grants a point against cereals, their high sugar. The next sentence turns with "But" to the cereals' value as a source of iron. Granting a point before reversing it is concession, so "Admittedly" is correct.

A.why: The cereals' sugar content doesn't result from the researchers' finding. Nothing in the previous sentences causes it.

C.why: The sugar content is not an example of the surprising answer. The surprise is the iron finding that comes after "But."

D.why: "Similarly" signals a parallel point. The sugar sentence is set up to be reversed by the "But" that follows, and that pattern calls for a concession word.
